item.title: The Voodoo Wiimote
item.description: The fun goes far beyond the game itself.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: A Nintendo Wii remote which acts as a voodoo doll on whomever or whatever its user is thinking about, so long as:

  • The Wii console the remote is paired to is powered on.
  • The remote is not connected to a Nunchuk peripheral.
  • The remote’s batteries are at least half full.

Central Narrative: A Nintendo Wii console was hooked up to a break room TV at Site-23. Almost immediately after, a researcher suffered severe injuries when one of the console’s remotes was sent flying into the TV. A security officer ordered for the console to be removed and disposed of, but submitted the previously mentioned remote to the labs for research. Soon after this, the object was registered as an SCP.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The Wii remote is mysterious in that there is very little potential for explaining its anomalous properties, and that it has potential use to the Foundation as a means of keeping peace at its sites.

Additional Notes: I wasn’t able to find any SCPs similar to this concept, so I was hoping critics could let me know if there are.

item.title: The Hungry Computer
item.description: Any criticism welcome.
item.content:encoded:
Item#: SCP-XXXX

Object Class: Safe

Containment Procedures: SCP-XXXX is stored at Site-23 in a standard anomalous object containment room that is 6m x 6m x 10m. The room is to be visually surveyed 24 hours a day. The anomalous object containment room is to be locked with a biometric lock that is coded to Level 3 and above. Any contact with SCP-XXXX is to be done with full body coverings. Gloves are 100% necessary if full body coverings are unavailable in an emergency.

Description: SCP-XXXX is a standard computer array that consists of one (1) unbranded monitor, one day (1) unbranded mouse, one (1) unbranded keyboard, and one (1) unbranded computer tower. SCP-XXXX appears to be a completely normal computer set-up that runs at standard levels for such a device at initial observation. Personnel interacting with SCP-XXXX cannot derive any difference between SCP-XXXX and a non-anomalous computer array. SCP-XXXX anomalous property can be observed when opening the computer case. The inner workings of SCP-XXXX are completely biological. The exterior “shell” is made up of chitin and bone. SCP-XXXX's tower has a heart that pumps blood throughout the biological “circuitry” of SCP-XXXX. Inside of the case additionally contains portions of brain tissue. These sections of brain tissue seem to be the major component to SCP-XXXX's memory and processing. There are additionally some small, unidentified organs inside SCP-XXXX that require further study to ascertain their purpose, such as bladders of unknown fluid, and small portions that appear to be keratin without a clear function. SCP-XXXX does not require any external power. As to how SCP-XXXX is functional without a source of power is unknown. Anyone wearing gloves can open the case and handle SCP-XXXX without triggering SCP-XXXX's consumption state (See SCP-XXXX-1.a) SCP-XXXX has been known to bleed if some of the softer interior is lacerated or punctured. These lacerations or punctures will heal at a rate that is normal for biological entities. SCP-XXXX appears to be vulnerable to any and all circumstances that would harm any other biological entity unless damage caused is to the exterior. Any scratches and divots appearing in SCP-XXXX's “carapace” or case seem to be permanent with the only exception is a complete puncture. The interior will heal leaving a mark where it was punctured.

SCP-XXXX-1.a. Dr. Tam’s research into SCP-XXXX’s consumption process and status.

One (1) D-Class (D-15893) was told to sit in front of SCP-XXXX and research a topic of his choosing. After a defined amount of time, SCP-XXXX began consumption.

1.) SCP-XXXX's keyboard and mouse produce microscopic "hooks" that attach to the user.

2.) SCP-XXXX's keyboard and mouse then produce a flesh-like covering that starts to envelope the user. These also have microscopic hooks that keep the user (here on referred to as victim) from escaping.

3.) SCP-XXXX will then produce a toxin that has an anesthetic effect. This toxin will also start to dissolve any biological material it comes into contact with.

4.) The additional components of SCP-XXXX begin consuming and joining together, SCP-XXXX has no semblance of its initial state and appears as a fleshy mass.

5.) After the victim is completely enveloped, SCP-XXXX will dissolve the victim completely returning to its previous state until another victim attempts to use SCP-XXXX.

6.) After approximately 5 hours SCP-XXXX will then eject a disk from its previously empty disk drive. The contents of the disk are described below.

7.) SCP-XXXX seems to produce no solid waste after consumption but a heavy smell of *"burnt hair"* can be derived while SCP-XXXX is in the final stages of consumption. Since SCP-XXXX doesn't grow in size and only produces the aforementioned CD, it is unclear what happens to most of the mass consumed by SCP-XXXX's.

+ Contents of Ejected Disk
– hide block

Side Research Notes: SCP-XXXX-A1: Contents of Disk The contents of the disk ejected by SCP-XXXX after consumption can be played on any standard CD drive device. It is unknown how SCP-XXXX produces the materials needed to produce a completely normal Compact Disk. When the CD is placed in any CD drive one must navigate to the file location. Once the file is opened, there is a standard word document. Inside this document is the complete genetic make-up of the victim consumed. Researchers theorize that this could potentially be used to clone the consumed victim. After a thorough study of the CD by renowned SCP biological engineer, Dr. Darren [REDACTED], it appears that some of the genetic make up shows signs of degradation. This indicates that this particular genetic code is representative of the consumed victim at the exact age they were when consumed. The reason SCP-XXXX's CD's are not given an SCP designation is due to the fact that this file can be removed or erased from the CD and then can be used as any other blank CD.

+ Approx. time table of Consumption process
– hide block

Approximate Time Summery of SCP-XXXX’s Consumption:

0:00 - D-15893 told to sit.

0:47 - D-15893 begins research into “orca whales”. First contact with SCP-XXXX reported.

4:37 - D-15893 noticed hands were stuck to SCP-XXXX

6:12 - SCP-XXXX is seen starting to expand.

15:42 - D-15893 is approx. 50% enveloped by SCP-XXXX

28:19 - SCP-XXXX has completely enveloped D-15893

32:47 - Struggling inside SCP-XXXX has ceased.

45:55 - SCP-XXXX began retracting.

48:02 - Smell described as “burnt hair” begins to permeate the testing lab.

59:35 - SCP-XXXX once again appears in its default form.

+ Addendum: Recovery Notes
- hide this content

Addendum: Recovery Notes** SCP-XXXX was found in the basement of ████████, a known rapist and murderer, located in ████████, WA on the date ██/██/████. Found with SCP-XXXX were also several corpses of ████████ victims. It is unknown if SCP-XXXX was a normal computer that was transformed via an unknown cause or was built with the biological material from the corpses around it via an unknown builder. During ████████ arrest, he stated *"What the ████ is that thing! How did it get into my basement?!"* indicating that ████████ was not responsible for SCP-XXXX's presence. SCP recovery teams were called by Agent ████████ who was inserted into the ████████ ████████ Agency at the time undercover. After ████████ was detained by local law enforcement, Agent ████████ was part of the team conducting the crime scene investigation and found SCP-XXXX. SCP-XXXX was found feeding on the corpses in the basement when SCP Agent ████████ found it. This was vital in the recovery process as it led to no loss of life recovering SCP-XXXX. All parties present except SCP personnel were given Class D amnestics.

O5 command statement;
*"We have learned all we need to learn about how SCP-XXXX eats living things. I see no reason to waste more D-Class persons to feed it. I think the next step should be to let it sit in its containment and see if the power begins to fail. If that's the case, we'll "feed" it and see if that's what gives it power. Being clear, I DO NOT want you to let it die. Have a D-Class ready in case of an emergency feeding."*

Researcher Aaron ████████ appealed to change status of SCP-XXXX from Euclid to Safe as *"It seems the only danger is when someone touches it"*. Appeal is approved

item.description: Anti-memetic glasses that explain the SCP universe's interaction with the law of conservation of mass

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: When worn, you are put in an anti-memetic state and, when viewing any anomaly that seemingly creates matter or energy, you will see a rubber wire leading out of it and into the sky.

Central Narrative: The foundation interacts with the 'electricity' that comes from these wires, until eventually they receive an invoice from the 'Electric Company' advising them to cease experimentation. They are successful in the creation of numerous useful anomalous devices before eventually, a 'Technician' appears in the site and retrieves the glasses before amnesticizing the foundation staff and deleting the file, which is found in data-backlogs by MTF-Rho 9. The item is considered neutralized for the time being.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The file is seemingly still anti-memetic and one needs to be conditioned using memetic images to view it. The underlying narrative of a foundation existing above the foundation responsible for the empowering of Anomalous items is the main hook of the article. Another piece of the puzzle is added to the mystery of where the energy for anomalies come from, with more room for expansion.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The origin of the parasites are unknown. There are currently 110 encounters on the foundation record.

item.title: The Perfectionist
item.description: A humanoid entity with a slight narcissistic attitude paired with an ability to mess with minds. (Seeking critique, as this will be my first idea on the site)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: This SCP is a humanoid entity with an unspecified or no gender, this SCP has its own anomalous property that make others 'listen' to it in a way. With its inhuman looks and narcissistic personality it caused a few problems…

Central Narrative: When a staff member found this SCP roaming the streets it was shouting at someone and then killed that someone while showing itself under the hood. Only to be caught detained shortly after by the staff member who was watching this unfold. It is now being held and contained, but makes trouble about being perfect and such often. Not much is known about the SCP, except for things like its ability to 'trick' the human mind, but it is thought to be from another place, planet, or possibly even universe, the Foundation cannot specify except the fact that it knows what it is, and possibly where it is from. Yet it will not comply or tell them either, as this was tried and failed.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This SCP can use its words to make people listen to it, it can somehow make people listen when it brings up something that a person wants, and tells them (The person) what to do to get it, making them do something that them in their right mind wouldn't, like going closer to said SCP. The effect that it gives needs to be tested on a bit more, as the Foundation doesn't know if it is explainable scientifically as of yet. The ability, or anomalous effect, the SCP has is connected to its nickname and personality, since it has slightly hinted at it, as those who are perfect do not have greed or something they want, this SCP may 'want' something but it does not think like that, it thinks that it can get it because it is perfect. And if the anomalous effect is connected, that means it has no sins or anything imperfect, from its point of view, maybe meaning if you do something that counts as bad or imperfect, also in its point of view, it may be able to get into your head.

Additional Notes: I'm not good at explaining ability's or anything of the sort, and this is my first ever SCP idea I'm putting here, so I would like good feedback on what I should change, or a different thing I should do.

item.title: Reanimating Elephant Graveyards
item.description: Every few decades an elephant graveyard reawakens, taking on humanoid forms
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout (Optional): Mostly the usual shtick, might include interview logs and/or discovery logs. This part isn't fleshed out yet and can still change a lot.

Elevator Pitch: All elephant graveyards are anomalous, the skeletons in them inevitably coming to live every 40-70 years. The living dead results reassemble themselves in a humanoid shape and move in a specific direction for 15 minutes before then falling apart again and repeating the process 40-70 years later.
The place they are moving towards is an obscure part of Russia where other elephant skeletons have already been stacked up many meters high in an intricate shape.
There also may be a secondary effect to the living skeletons that causes people to hallucinate, blurring the details of the encounter.

Central Narrative: No concrete narrative but rather the idea that the public is aware of the elephant skeletons, considering them an urban legend. The foundation would then have to base its procedures on that fact and make sure the people believe the scp to be a hoax.
The event's age would also be explored as parallels are drawn between it and cave drawings or alleged cyclops encounters.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The main hook would be the vague knowledge that the public has of the scp, as well as the weirdness of the event itself. Similar ideas have been made into scps before but I believe that the specifics make my concept stand out among the others.

Additional Notes: The whole "humanoid elephant skeleton" idea is largely based on the theory that people used to mistake elephant skulls for those of cyclopes, creating that myth in the first place.
Specific numbers and values were mostly chosen to make the scp as annoying to contain as possible(a bit silly in hindsight).
I know that the idea still needs a good amount of polishing. I hope I can turn it into something sort of worthwhile in the end.

item.title: The Rube Effect
item.description: Woman evades death by a string of 'random' events that neutralizes immediate threats.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Drama/Emotional, Comedy

Page Layout: Test and incident logs to be included. I intend to cross refence other works, but would like to ask permission from other authors before I commit to that.

Elevator Pitch: Woman is infected with a "virus" of sorts that neutralizes nearby deadly threats with 'events' that work on a similar principle to the butterfly effect or a Rube Goldberg machine. It can manipulate any non-organic material to complete an event. The woman is incredulously unaware of her anomalous properties.

Central Narrative: The virus is contagious but this is unknown by the Foundation at the time of the article's writing. Its effects are efficient but subtle. The Subject was the child of two researchers who were killed in a containment breach. She's sent to live at the School for Children of Prominence. A boarding school/orphanage for children of Foundation personnel. She is notably idiotic and it amazes her teachers that she actually graduates. Once she starts working for the Foundation as a junior researcher, her peers are dumbfounded that despite lacking all common sense she has yet to die. This prompts an investigation and her eventual classification as an SCP. After the article is submitted for review the higher ups begin to doubt the judgement of the lead researcher and try to have the SCP declassified due to 'lack or sufficient anomalous evidence'. The lead researcher is shunned and dives into a depressed drunken stupor. It remains to be seen if the Foundation will continue the research and discover how to harness the power of this virus.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The virus isn't all powerful and it wont infect just anyone. It's host can still be injured and it will not prevent death due to biological means such as old age or venom. It is, however, very good at keeping its host alive. The Foundation would kill to have something like this for all of their field agents.

item.title: Two Dimensional Love
item.description: Sounds good on paper, doesn't it?
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Elevator Pitch:

  • A bloodstained kirigami paper doll 1.56 meters in length drawn on to resemble a female human in an anime style, wearing gothic "lolita" style attire. Edges of the paper are abnormally sharp and capable of inflicting wounds on contact far greater than the amount of pressure and composition of the fibers would allow for. Subject is inanimate but believed to be sentient.
  • Any male who enters the doll's line of "sight" has an approximate 3% chance of being imprinted on, upon which its effect manifests. Upon entering REM sleep, the victim has a 50% chance to enter a state similar to sleep paralysis, in which a vision of the doll will appear to them and gently caress them, leaving deep wounds. This process is painless but can still result in complications from blood loss or infection.
  • Any female (biological or transgender) the victim interacts with that is not of blood relation enters a similar state the next time they sleep in which they are executed in a manner similar to the Chinese Lingchi. This process is not painless.
  • If the victim has not expired after a period of seven days, they will progress to Stage 2 in which they have an approximate 12.5% chance of the doll attempting to copulate with them. This normally results in death by blood loss. Only one affected victim can exist at a time.

Central Narrative: Article proceeds normally, with an addendum regarding its recovery from the belongings of a deceased Japanese man implied to be its creator after his "suicide" in police custody. Several experiment logs are listed near the end with the Foundation using D-Class to determine how it works.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Final experiment log has the Foundation manage to keep a D-Class alive long enough to describe Stage 2 to them. He explains that the doll, which was silent before then, kept repeating a single phrase: "Mō kakkoīdesu ka?" (Japanese for "Are we cool yet?")

item.title: My First SCP Idea: The Wooden Vulture
item.description: A "living" caved wooden vulture that eats human flesh
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes, but I don’t expect it’ll get greenlit at the first go. I’m mostly looking for feedback right now.

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (optional): Unsure

Page Layout (optional): Contains containment procedures, description, discovery, test logs, and maybe even a cross-link.

Elevator Pitch: A “living” carved wooden vulture that feeds on human corpses. It will get “hungry” after 24 hours, which is when it will start searching for corpses to feed on. If it hasn't eaten for 36 to 48 hours, it will enter a frenzy, which makes it exponentially stronger and more aggressive. In this state, it will eat people alive in order to satiate its “hunger.” In this state, it will even ignore any dead human meat and go straight for the nearest living human.

Central Narrative: What is speculated to be its first victim was a woodworker specializing in custom statues. It's believed that the vulture killed the victim as opposed to feasting on their corpse.

Ever since the first body was found, mutilated and dismembered, many more bodies soon popped up with similar disfigurements. This caused many problems for local law enforcement.

The Foundation stepped in when a video of the creature was brought into the hands of the police. What caught their eye was the unnatural material it seemed to be made out of.

The Foundation easily caught it with the scent of human flesh, but they did not fully understand its eating habits at the time, nor did they anticipate the consequences of the lack of understanding that they had. They tried to feed it animal carcasses. They were able to keep it for 2 days before it escaped in one of its “frenzy states” and ate a Class-D Personnel alive. It was soon recaptured and given human flesh to eat. It hasn't escaped, nor tried to escape since then.

Presently, the SCP sits in its containment cell, docile. It is given a pound of human flesh every 24 hours. It seems to be satiated.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The simple but unique appearance and description combined with the grotesque nature of its feeding.

Additional Notes: “How's The Foundation able to obtain the human flesh that they feed the SCP?”

The Foundation has struck a deal with a nearby city using one of their front companies, which allows them access to unwanted or unclaimed dead bodies. They also have access to the corpses of people who have donated their bodies to science.

I’d be willing to delete the “escaped and ate a guard” part to make The Foundation not look like idiots.

If this ever gets greenlit I’d like to include a brief cross-link to SCP-3847 if possible.

item.title: SCP Concept: Life is short
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: A humanoid SCP that is given birth to by a randomly picked woman in labour across the world, however the SCP will only live for 24 hours and when it dies another woman gives birth to it. It varies gender between times.

Central Narrative: A woman is in a hospital, going through labour, and finally gives birth to her child. She's happy, but something feels off, the child doesn't scream and both her and the doctors are shocked and panicked, until the baby speaks to them and wiggles itself free. When on the ground, it introduces itself to them before being taken to a special room in the hospital. The child doesn't understand them and tries to leave the room before being studied by doctors, amongst them an undercover Field Agent from the Foundation. It soon explains itself to the team and it's able to escape from the hospital. After that it seeks new places to go, observe, study and learn. This SCP was then reported to the Foundation and later was observed and studied a few times by the Staff.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The most interesting thing about this anomaly is that the SCP can remember past life experiences, it can grow very intelligent and wise over years and aqquire knowledge for many things, even as a newborn, and it's believed that it's main purpose is to learn. The only limits it has is it's very short life and it's physical form when both very young and very old. The SCP is also never born with any defficiency. What's also interesting about this SCP is that currently it poses no threats to humans, however, as it grows more intelligent there is a possibility of it attempting to end humans.

item.title: The Copy - Idea
item.description: I like to write and draw. Got bored so I thought why not?
item.content:encoded:
Nickname: "The Copy".
Class: Safe Euclid

I've always had an interest in writing and I've have been writing for a couple years now, on an app called Wattpad. My writing has flaws but bare with me please. And let me know if an idea like it has already been used, I'd hate to feel as if someone already had the idea and I was taking it.

"Copy" is a very strange female humanoid with charcoal coloured skin around the head and neck. The rest fades into very pale and normal skin. It's hair is pure white and it has no recognizable facial features, even when direct light is on it's face. It's movements are slow but, despite it's lack of eyes, seems to know exactly where it is going.

Copy was found standing on a bridge near an extremely old forest. It made no effort to run or even hide from personnel. However, once they were close enough, It slowly pointed to a particularly dark clearing in the distance of the forest. Upon investigating, a body of a female was found wearing the exact same clothes as Copy (a stripped shirt falling off her shoulders and a light grey, 2 tier skirt). The body's skull had been removed but the rest of the body was still there. The identity of the corpse couldn't be discovered but it's killer was nearby and terminted. It was apprehended and brought in for questioning. However, to question it, you need to spend longer than necessary with it, as explained below.

The most unique thing about Copy is the way it manages to speak. While it cannot speak on it's own terms, it can mimic another person's facial features (including skin) and voice. The face is copied while it's hair and the rest of it's body remains the same. To answer the Foundation's questions, she will copy the face and words said to her in the exact tone and pitch of the person in front of her. This lead to quite a bit of irritation when talking to it, unless you are not easily angered, as the foundation had no idea how to get answers out of it. Than all of a sudden it spoke back, answering as many questions as it could with the words it's interviewer spoke. The way it spoke back is by using the words spoken to her, just chopped up (think of video game modders, occasionally they have to cut up NPC dialogue to make voices), to make legible sentences. The issue is that once the interviewer has stopped talking to it, it removes any source of conversation it previously had with the interviewer, so no matter how long the foundation spoke with Copy, she would always forget. And if too many people are speaking at once, she will manage to form all faces on it's face and overlap all the words speaking.

On quite a few occasions, 073 was the one to be sent to question it, due to his genuine friendliness and calm personality. 073
spent 3 hours speaking to Copy and had quite a few questions answered. I imagine it like this:

073: Hello
Copy: Hello
073: How are you?
Copy: How are you?
073: Are you…Copying me?
Copy: Are you…Copying me?
073: Okay…What's your name?
Copy: Copy. What's your name?
073: Cain, or 073, if you prefer
Copy: Cain
073: Yes, that's my name
Copy: How are you?

Or something like that. I imagine if you talk enough than it is more than happy to talk back.

It isn't at all aggressive towards personnel and quite passive about aggressive things that are said to it. It's interesting to watch people insult it for the insult to bounce back at them.

I set it to Euclid because when a breach occurs, she flips out, destroying her containment cell and anyone who enters while this is happening. So far, I'd imagine only a small amount of lives cover her hands, so when she appears agitated, just leave her be until she literally knocks herself out.

Central narrative & Hook/attention-grabber
Thanks for clicking

Central Narrative:
The basic idea of this, is that the SCP is from another universe. In that said universe the main Gods and deities exist (the ones mentioned previously) each one basically owning a portion of the world (like the Olympians getting Greece and the Egyptians getting Egypt) and making it their own with their subsequent powers. But after millions of years of the gods and other smaller deities ruling the world, the humans become fed up. They band together combining magic and science to create SCP-XXXX (no number) this entity is made to destroy these “Gods” one by one and free man kind. But little do they know that with every god, deity and demi-god it kills it gains a little bit of humanity, emotions and all. Eventually after killing and devouring every last God, it has become essentially human in emotional terms. But when it returns and is told the kill code (intended to kill him and rid the world of the last god), it lives and realizes that they tried to kill him after all it did for them. It begins to attack the humans, but they open a wormhole and it is sent to the scp universe, where it gets to mainly participate in tests and experiments, as it cant really be contained. But one scientist is determined to contain it even though it is harmless to the SCP universes humans. So with the approval of the O5 council, gases are tested on the entity. Eventually figuring out how to sedate it. A collar is then attached to it as a way of semi containing it, but the scientist that made the request isn't happy about this compromise and creates a gas that can knock the entity out for a thousand years. Obviously the ethics committee and the O5 are not happy about this and subsequently decommission the gas. But the doctor ingests a vial and antagonizes the entity, making it aggressive and begin to hate humans again. finally it kills the doctor and the gas inside him is release, knocking him out. the foundation knows that this entity is too dangerous to wake up due to its mental state (observed with brain wave scans) so they decide to, against the ethics committees judgment, store it indefinitely in a humanoid containment locker at site 132.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
Whats special about this idea is that we get to see the building of a God from another world and eventually becoming a man (through interviews and other stories relayed by SCP-XXXX). And after he learns about being human he instantly doesn't want to be one because of what his people did to it. So it's like a betrayal story that makes people feel empathy for it, then sadness as it gets betrayed again in the SCP universe. I'd add mystery to this by giving it redacted details

I would love this idea to reach draft status, as I have had this idea for a novel for a long time and I thought it would be great to get feedback from here. And if it became an scp. It would make a great story character to have in many different stories.

It caught his eye because of the realistic landscape of the snow globe, but when the gift was opened a half a month later, there were certain features that had appeared on the landscape that the foundation member were not there when he purchased the globe, such as a crop field and a few crude houses. The foundation personnel brought the globe to the foundation and has since been on 24-hour observation by a camera which has documented the progress of the internal civilization.

+ show block
– hide block

While on an expedition/hunting an SCP/recovering from a containment breach, a foundation team reported the immediate disappearance of a team member, as if he had been swallowed up by the air in front of him. As foundation command began to question the team on the specifics of the disappearance immediately following the incident, they could not recall the existence of the team member at all, and foundation records of the team suggested likewise. The identification of a disappearance was nonetheless recorded. The anomalous properties of the snow globe were only discovered when the camera observing the snow globe recorded a flare gun fire from within the forest of the globe approximately 3 minutes after the disappearance of the team member. Currently no attempts have been made from the inhabitants of the interior to communicate with the foundation, and it is unknown whether the victims are aware of their situation. When foundation personnel revisited the site of the disappearance, nothing occurred, and the source of victimization remains unknown.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: While the idea of a miniature self-contained civilization isn’t completely unique, the events that resulted in the discovery of the anomaly is testament to the aptitude of the foundation. Regardless, it was a fun and engaging idea to develop.

item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: The anomaly was a former channel on the media site “YouTube” that was active from 11/15/19 to 11/15/20 exactly one year from its creation.

The channel uploaded what would seem like fun original content but was littered with cognitohazardous material that has now been completely neutralized. Two humanoids are present in every video and host the channel. Both entities are almost identical to two other famous people but are not the same people.

Subjects who view any of the 365 videos are instantly met with a clock that counts down starting from 365:00:00. The anomaly’s effects immediate initiate at the start of every video by infecting and manipulating the subject’s mind making them perceive the two entities as gods and begin to worship the two entities in nonsensical and sometimes violent ways. Afflicted subjects attempt to spread the anomaly through social media and other chat related applications.

The anomaly can not be deleted directly by YouTube since attempts to do so crash all electronic devices.

The two entities seen in every video seem to not be a part of our dimension but from another reality. Since they cannot be located and have been seen with anomalous items that do cannot exist in our reality.
Central Narrative: The Narrative would dictate all of the foundations attempts to neutralize the anomaly and work with YouTube to contain the anomaly from spreading. Millions of viewers have already been infected by the anomaly and spread of the anomaly drastically increases. The Foundation worries that an AK end of the world scenario could occur as tens of millions of people rapidly fall under the anomaly’s influence. As governments collapse and people perform violent rituals in the streets the channel finally reaches its climatic end

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Based on a real experiment conducted on the same website.

Additional Notes: The central narrative would begin by detailing the small amount of infection but slowly starts getting worse and worse until the end. Not all details described here it would be too long.

Elevator Pitch: A phenomenon that manifests near the locations and annual anniversaries of famous battles. Terrain and weather in the affected area reconfigure to match the original battle, and invisible and intangible entities manifest to reenact it, along with the appropriate military hardware, which is visible but still intangible. The Foundation initially thinks that these entities are ghosts, but they eventually notice that they’re sentient and aware of their surroundings, then attempts to make contact. The Foundation briefly speaks with the entities, enough to realize some humorous misconceptions the entities have about how human war works in three-dimensional space. Eventually, the entities manifest to reenact a battle that never happened. When the Foundation points this out, the entities realize they’re in the wrong universe and demanifest, never to return.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: The Foundation first discovers this phenomenon when it manifests near a populated area. There’s a log of notable manifestations (current list includes the Battles of Bull Run/Manassas, Hastings, Rorke’s Drift, and Megiddo, plus a prehistoric conflict between Homo sapiens and Neanderthals and a battle between the Mongols and Daevites). The log notes illustrate the Foundation’s dawning awareness of the entities’ sentience and attempts to interact, concluding with a final log of a manifestation somewhere in the Southern US that doesn’t correspond with any known battle. There are two addenda after that: one chronicling a humorous interaction between a Foundation personnel and one of the entities and one chronicling the final encounter with the anomaly, during which they realize they’re in the wrong place (“We’re in the wrong universe, you stupid idiot!”).

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The bait-and-switch of anomalies that seem to be ghosts but are actually slightly confused extradimensional war-reenacters is an amusing twist. I also intend to imply or even crosslink that the nonexistent battle is the one described by SCP-592. I plan to eventually write a Tale about the universe full of faceless people described by that book and encountered in SCP-970.

Additional Notes: I’m not sure if I should have the anomalies manifest at the actual locations of the battles or on some shapeshifting island or something out in the middle of nowhere. Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a Euclid-class collection of parasitic donor organs that are capable of osmotic extracellular digestion. Individual "fragments" of SCP-XXXX possess passive, non-lethal cognitohazardous properties.

Central Narrative: The Tainted Saint Collection is the first entry in a wider narrative I have planned. It's centered around the research of Dr. Lee Elliot, an ex-field agent with an interest in SCPs that can manipulate organic matter. I intend for this narrative to begin (temporally) with a different SCP, an incident report, and a Tale. However, this SCP seemed like a better place to start in practice since it's easier to pitch.

+ show block
– hide block

The report starts out normal, with little off-kilter details sprinkled in to breed unease. Note, I described SCP-XXXX as a collection of donor organs in the intro here, but in the article itself that information will not be revealed until the description section. By the time the reader reaches that point, I want them to be hyperaware of the danger associated with even brief contact so the reveal that they were implanted into people hits as hard as possible.

Beyond that, the bulk of the article's narrative will follow the background of each fragment individually, outlining their quirks. SCP-XXXX-B, for example, kills its hosts within a few days, whereas SCP-XXXX-A remained inside the same host for six months. At the end, I plan on including a brief interview between SCP-XXXX-A's ex-host and Dr. Elliot. Lastly, I'll include a short lab report detailing a non-lethal vivisection of SCP-XXXX-A that ended up costing Dr. Elliot his left eye. Spoiler alert: fragments of SCP-XXXX are immobile by choice, not biology.

Hook/Attention Grabber: They're carnivorous donor organs with cognitohazardous properties. I know I'd read an article about that.

Additional Notes: I have way too much experience writing formal academic prose, so my main concern is getting the lore/terminology right. When d-class are sent to investigate with less specialized transmission equipment, they discover a seemingly endless series of waiting rooms, storage areas, backstages, and stages filled with decaying props. The props and hints towards the play performed vary wildly from room to room, and the one room the d-class seem to find but not explore is a basement, from where the creature emerges and kills most of the d-class in the exploration party; those who survived ended up proving the contagious capabilities of the fungus inside and were terminated.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The creature within stitches all those who it manages to catch onto itself, through a redacted procedure observed through drone observation (exploration logs). And it is stated that there was one time the creature actually managed to breach containment, and in the time it took Foundation personnel to find out where the creature had gone, it managed to decimate the entire population of a city, level several buildings, and almost open a portal into an unknown dimension possibly filled with creatures alike it. The creature’s sudden increase in capabilities when outside containment proved that the building’s anomalous properties seem to aid in the containment of the creature.

Additional Notes: The Article’s series of addendums let it be known that the creature, the last times it’s been seen by personnel within the building, has been covered in water or has left humid footprints. item.content:encoded:
A creature with a boundless hatred of sexual predators uses a combination of mental manipulation and shapeshifting to lure and brutally murder predators. The predator of predators

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror

Idea Pitch
Idea Pitch


Elevator Pitch: The basic idea for this SCP is a creature who commits acts of horrific violence against people who are considered to be one of the most repulsive kind of people alive (sexual predators). In order to challenge the common idea amongst some people that "evil people" such as sexual predators (rapists, paedophiles, gropers, those who use power to pressure others into sex) deserve no mercy and the death penalty. By having a humanoid creature that symbolises human hatred committing acts of sadistic violence with non-human apendages I hope to express how the act of killing is inhumane.

Central Narrative: The police are investigating a string of murders, the victims are all men and women either accused or found guilty of sexual abuse. The only other thing connecting the victims is that they were all last spotted with a different person who the police can find no records proving they exist. As there are so far 15 victims along with 15 people seen with them with no proof of existence it has the police both confused and at a loss for what to do.

A Foundation mole inside the LAPD brings the case to the attention of the Foundation who find the circumstances suspicious and decide to investigate themselves. Eventually after tracking potential victims in the area they catch the creature in the act, it has lured the Reigional Manager of a local tobacco company (who has been using his power to sexually harrass, grope and pressure young female employees and interns into sex) into bed. Only to use non human apendages to slit the man's throat and begin mutilating his corpse.

The Foundation capture and contain the creature, bringing it back for further study. Where it's psychology, biology, nature, abilites of mental manipulation and shapeshifting are researched by the foundation.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A humanoid creature is enacting something people often fantisize about, killing sex offenders. However the hateful, apathetic and sadistic nature of the SCP leads the audience to reflect on thier attitudes towards the death penalty as a reflection of their own feelings towards those they hate is represented as monster.

Additional Notes: The subject of sexual assualt and abuse is a very sensetive issue, this SCP idea is not intended to make light of these issues. Rather show them for what they are; evil and dispicable. As well helping readers to vent thir frustrations about these issues by seeing predators get served unmerciful justice. It's not my intention to make survivors relive their trauma so if this idea makes it to draft a trigger warning will be provided.
